definitions.gloss: to come to mind; to occur to
definitions.explanation: For an idea, memory, or image to suddenly enter one's thoughts.

examples.japanese: いい{考|かんが}えが{思|おも}い{浮|う}かんだ。
examples.english: A good idea came to mind.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{顔|かお}が{思|おも}い{浮|う}かばない。
その{言葉|ことば}を{聞|き}いて、{故郷|こきょう}の{風景|ふうけい}が{思|おも}い{浮|う}かんだ。
examples.english: Hearing those words, the scenery of my hometown came to mind.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive)
Pair: {思|おも}い{浮|う}かべる (transitive - to recall, picture)
Pattern: Xが{思|おも}い{浮|う}かぶ

VERB STRUCTURE:
{思|おも}う (to think) + {浮|う}かぶ (to float up) = to float up in one's mind

ASPECT (ている):
{思|おも}い{浮|う}かんでいる - is in one's mind (continuous state)

NEGATIVE FORM:
{思|おも}い{浮|う}かばない - can't think of, doesn't come to mind
This negative form is very common when expressing inability to remember or imagine.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頭|あたま}に{浮|う}かぶ - to come to mind
- {思|おも}い{出|だ}す - to remember, recall
